notes: Harney & Sons names Zhenghe alongside Fu'an, so it is added to the region. Added the Wikidata alias and common variants. The Wikipedia altitude and 1700/300-year claims were kept out of the card as unsourced.

notes: Hedged the undocumented claims that Guangxi is one of the biggest sources of fake Jin Jun Mei and that a cheap gold one is very likely Gui Hong, plus the 1960s start and 'one of the best-value' superlative. None of them could be found in a readable source.
doubt: Could not read any page that uses 桂红 as a product name (Baidu Baike refused; searches returned nothing on it). The tea may be a shorthand for Guangxi black in general rather than an established name. Needs a human check.

notes: Added the traditional form and a Russian variant to aliases. The state-farm dates in the card match the search text; Yunnan seed and the February to November picking season were not confirmed.

Added the traditional form. Lightly oxidised overstated it: sources place it at the low end for Wuyi, not at light-oolong levels. The earlier origin-account fix agrees with a Chinese overview, which gives both sites.

Removed the early 1980s selection date: the source read gives only the 1996 approval. Hedged the claim that this cultivar lies behind most Wuyi Qi Lan, found in no source read. Added the Pengxi and tea-station details from the source and the traditional form.
Removed the early 1960s date and softened the flat identity with Lingtou Dancong and the claim of sprouting earlier than any other dancong: none could be confirmed in a page that opened.
doubt: Possible duplicate of lingtou-dancong: this card itself treats the two as one plant under two names, a link no source read here confirms or refutes. Needs a human decision on merging.
